title: Demand · NREL OEDI 8562 · state
description: Highest hourly electricity demand of each state in 2023, in MW, from the modeled county demand profiles of OEDI submission 8562 (National Laboratory of the Rockies, formerly NREL). The profiles of the state's counties are added up hour by hour, and the highest of the 8,760 hourly totals is taken. This is not the sum of the county peaks, because counties reach their peaks at different hours. Alaska and Hawaii are not covered and have empty values.

coverage.geography: Contiguous United States and the District of Columbia
known_gaps: Alaska and Hawaii are not covered.

County demand is modeled, not metered: in this dataset, retail sales reported by utilities are totaled by state and allocated to counties by each county's share of the state population. The state is therefore closer than the county to the level at which the source starts.
The 49 state peaks add up to 810,503.2 MW, less than the 822,740.1 MW of the county peaks. For each state the peak is between 94.4% (California) and 100% of the sum of its county peaks.
The hour of each state's peak is not a field of the layer; state_reconciliation.csv gives it in UTC.

verification.method: The hourly profiles of each state's counties are added up by script and the yearly maximum is taken. The same run recomputed the county peaks and matched the published values of version 0.1.0 in every county. For every state the build checked that its peak is not below its largest county peak and not above the sum of its county peaks. No value was re-checked by a person or by an agent. The automated checks listed below were run on every build.

automated_checks.description: SHA-256 of every input file was computed at the start and again at the end of the build; they match.
The file has exactly one row for each of the 51 USA ADM1 units of the boundaries release; 49 are covered and 2 are not_covered with empty values.
Every unit_id of the layer exists in the boundaries release and no unit_id is repeated.
Columns of the CSV, GeoParquet and GeoJSON files equal fields[] in composition and order.
The sum of every numeric column read back from the published CSV equals the sum in the input table.
